title: Loglineage, Retention, Redaction, and SIEM Delivery Playbook (v0.1 Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures a combined approach for: 1) establishing a forward-compatible audit event envelope and versioning path (v1 -> v2 -> v3), 2) deterministic redaction and retention lifecycle, 3) RBAC v2 decision logging requirements, and 4) pragmatic delivery adapters for SIEM and evidence automation.

Audience and context:
- Primary: security engineers, compliance, observability engineers, and platform infra owners.
- This is intentionally lightweight and opinionated: we want an implementable shim that teams can adopt while we iterate on a canonical event store.

High-level design goals:
- Single canonical event envelope that can be translated to SIEM-friendly formats.
- Explicit schema_version field, stable compatibility guarantees (minor additive fields allowed, breaking changes require migration).
- Privacy-by-design: minimize PII in the canonical store, provide deterministic redaction for downstream correlation when needed.
- Traceability: every event carries lineage metadata so we can reconstruct derivation and TTL.
- Evidence automation: packageable artifacts (manifest + signed references) to support investigations and audits.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Canonical Envelope: the primary JSON structure we write to the audit store. Contains metadata, payload, rbac_decision, and lineage.
- Delivery Adapters: lightweight translators that convert the canonical envelope to SIEM (CEF, ECS, Splunk JSON) or to evidence bundles.
- Tombstone Event: a special envelope with op: "tombstone" used to mark deletion/retention expirations.
- Deterministic Hashing: keyed hash of redacted values (HMAC-SHA256 with KMS-managed salt) to allow correlation without storing raw PII.

Schema/Envelope (example)
Note: labels are descriptive. Fields may be omitted if empty; do not rename. Additive fields allowed.
{
  "event_id": "uuid-v4",
  "schema_version": "audit-envelope@v1",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-19T15:02:33Z",
  "tenant_id": "org_12345",
  "source": "api-gateway/us-east1",
  "region_hint": "us-east1",
  "operation": "model.invoke|resource.update|auth.check",
  "resource": "projects/prod/models/llama-70b/versions/2026-02-10",
  "actor": {
    "principal_id": "user_6789",
    "principal_type": "user|service",
    "display_name": "alice@acme.com"
  },
  "rbac_decision": {
    "allowed": true,
    "policy_id": "policy-33",
    "policy_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
    "reason": "matches-role-and-constraint",
    "constraints": ["ip_restriction:vpn-only","time_window:09-17"]
  },
  "change_set": {"before": "ref-obj-v1","after": "ref-obj-v2"},
  "sensitive_fields_redacted": ["request_body.user_email"],
  "redaction_map": {"request_body.user_email": "hmac:sha256:xyz"},
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://evidence-bucket/manifest-2026-02-19-evt.json"],
  "lineage": {"ingested_by": "audit-writer-v2","origin_event": "evt-abc123"},
  "ttl_hint": "P365D",
  "notes": "free-text for investigators"
}

(We will maintain a small registry mapping schema_version -> compatibility policy.)

Versioning notes (v1 -> v2 -> v3)
- v1: initial envelope above. Minimal required fields: event_id, schema_version, timestamp, tenant_id, operation, actor.
- v2: adds rbac_decision.policy_hash, redaction_map, evidence_refs, lineage.ingested_by. Backward compatible if consumers ignore new fields.
- v3: planned changes that may be incompatible: introduce binary blobs for attachments, deprecate display_name in actor and replace with actor_refs array for multi-principal events. Migration approach: dual-write for 90 days + shim translator for older consumers.

Compatibility guarantees: adopt semver-like rules for consumers:
- patch (v1.0.x): bugfixes and clarifications, no structural additions.
- minor (v1.x.0): additive fields allowed; old consumers must tolerate unknown fields.
- major (v2.0.0): breaking changes require a migration window and dual-write support. A deprecation header will be emitted for 60 days before major switch.

RBAC v2 logging requirements (what teams must log)
- Every authorization decision must produce an audit envelope with rbac_decision populated. Required fields: allowed (bool), policy_id, policy_hash, principal_id, principal_type, resource, decision_timestamp.
- Include context used in evaluation (constraints that matched). Do not include raw policy source—store policies in policy store and reference by id/hash.
- Policy_hash is critical for forensics: compute over normalized policy to prove what was evaluated.

PII redaction strategy
- Primary store: avoid storing raw PII where possible. For fields that must be recorded for traceability, store deterministic keyed HMAC values: hmac_sha256(tenant_salt || field_value). Tenant salt is retrieved from KMS; rotation strategy is documented elsewhere.
- For high-risk fields, persist only hashed value and schema pointers to original artifact (evidence_ref) instead of raw text.
- Redaction map: canonical envelope includes a redaction_map mapping original json-path -> token so investigators can correlate across events without raw data.
- Emergency unredaction: only via an evidence automation flow that requires: 2-person approval, signed request, and audit of KMS decrypt usage. This flow produces a signed evidence bundle with full chain-of-custody.

Retention lifecycle and tombstones
- TTL is tenant-visible (ttl_hint) but enforced by retention controller which writes a tombstone event before removal. Tombstone fields: event_id(original), tombstone_for: event_id, reason, purge_timestamp.
- Physical deletion pipeline reads tombstones and tenant retention policy and runs delete jobs for blobs (S3/GCS) and table rows.
- For evidence artifacts, we append a manifest entry with retention metadata and keep manifests immutable to support audits.

SIEM delivery adapters
- We support multiple adapters in parallel: NDJSON S3 buckets (rotated by hour), Kinesis passthrough (for AWS SIEM connectors), PubSub/LogSink for GCP, and a direct FluentD/Collector plugin.
- Adapter rules:
  - Normalize timestamp to epoch_millis and add siem_source_host.
  - Map canonical fields to ECS/CEF where possible. Keep original envelope in "raw_event" for full fidelity (if tenant allows).
  - For tenants with retained PII policies: the adapter will substitute redacted tokens in the exported fields and attach redaction_map metadata under a vendor-specific key.
- Rate and batching: adapters must respect tenant quotas and expose backpressure to the canonical writer (retryable batch writes).

Evidence automation and packaging
- When an investigator requests an artifact, the system creates an evidence bundle:
  - manifest.json (signed, includes list of event_ids, retrieval_time, requestor_id, approval_chain)
  - one or more ndjson files with raw or redacted events (depending on approval)
  - signed checksums and audit log of who accessed the bundle
- Bundles are stored in an immutable evidence bucket and referenced in evidence_refs in envelopes. Bundles are time-limited with signed URLs.

Operational runbook (quick steps)
- On suspected data exposure: set investigator_mode TTLs, escalate to retention controller, create evidence bundle with full raw events, start unredaction workflow if warranted.
- On schema change: open PR with schema diff, tag as minor/major, run translator job against canonical store to verify dual-write compatibility, update adapters.

Open design questions / TODOs
- Salt management: are per-tenant salts required or is a per-environment salt sufficient for our threat model? Can we offload to customer-managed keys for high-compliance tenants?
- Tombstone semantics: do we need to keep tombstones permanently for forensic indexing or can we garbage collect them after purge windows?
- Evidence bundle signing format: recommend JOSE signatures; need to align with legal for chain-of-custody.
- RBAC decision verbosity: how much of evaluation context is safe to include without duplicating policy text?

Immediate action items
- [ ] Align on schema_version naming convention (proposal: audit-envelope@v<major>). @Jordan to draft RFC by 2026-02-25.
- [ ] Implement adapter prototype: NDJSON S3 + Splunk HTTP connector. @Luis to own. ETA 2026-03-15.
- [ ] KMS salt rotation doc and emergency unredaction flow. @Sofia to draft legal/compliance checklist. ETA 2026-03-01.

Appendix: small example tombstone event
{
  "event_id": "tomb-2026-02-20-0001",
  "schema_version": "audit-envelope@v1",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-20T00:00:00Z",
  "tenant_id": "org_12345",
  "operation": "tombstone",
  "tombstone_for": "evt-9a7b6c",
  "reason": "retention-expired:365d",
  "purge_timestamp": "2026-02-20T00:05:00Z",
  "ingested_by": "retention-controller-v1"
}

Notes: keep this doc intentionally practical and lean — prefer concrete adapters and runbooks over theoretical taxonomy. We'll iterate after the initial implementation and record lessons in the RFC and Confluence.

End of draft.
